items.body: Review by Abrasmatheus — Wish You Were Here is one of those albums that does not need to be excessively complex to feel progressive. Released in 1975, it combines progressive rock, psychedelic rock, art rock and space rock into an incredibly cohesive and atmospheric experience. I would not consider it one of Pink Floyd's most overtly progressive albums, but its careful compositions, long instrumental developments, experimental production and thematic coherence make it a very strong progressive rock work.The atmosphere is probably the album's greatest strength. It is contemplative, melancholic, emotional and, at times, almost intellectual in the way its themes are presented. The production has aged remarkably well, with every instrument occupying its own space in the mix. The synthesizers and keyboards of Richard Wright are particularly impressive, adding an essential dimension to the album's sound.The centerpiece is undoubtedly "Shine On You Crazy Diamond", which I consider a masterpiece in its own right. I prefer to experience its different sections as one complete work rather than treating them as separate pieces. The song contains excellent instrumental development, especially in the guitars, drums and synthesizers. David Gilmour's guitar work is outstanding, combining technical ability with an enormous amount of emotional expression. Wright's keyboards are equally important, creating much of the psychedelic and spacious atmosphere that defines the piece.The emotional weight of "Shine On You Crazy Diamond" is also increased by its connection to Syd Barrett, whose work with Pink Floyd I greatly admire. Knowing that the song was written as a tribute to him gives the piece an additional emotional dimension. The feeling of loss and nostalgia is deeply present without overwhelming the music itself."Welcome to the Machine" is another major highlight. Its synthesizer work is simply magnificent, and the electronic textures create an almost mechanical atmosphere that perfectly complements the song's subject matter. The composition is less progressive in a traditional structural sense, but its sound design and atmosphere are remarkably creative. I would give the synthesizers an almost absurd 10/10 ? or, jokingly, 1,000,000/10. This is one of the clearest examples of how Pink Floyd could use studio production itself as part of the composition.The lyrics also contribute considerably to the album's thematic unity. Alongside the tribute to Syd Barrett, the record deals with the music industry and the way it can become destructive and dehumanizing. "Welcome to the Machine" and "Have a Cigar" are particularly effective in this regard. Even though these themes were written in the 1970s, they remain strikingly relevant today."Have a Cigar" is another very enjoyable track. Roy Harper's vocals work surprisingly well and have some similarities to Roger Waters' voice. The song is more accessible than some of the album's other material, but it still fits naturally into the overall concept.The title track, "Wish You Were Here", is probably the most commercially accessible song on the album. I personally rate it slightly below the other tracks, at 7/10, but it still serves an important role in the album as a whole. Its lyrics and emotional character provide another perspective on the themes of absence, loss and alienation.One of the things I appreciate most about Wish You Were Here is how naturally the tracks connect to each other. The album can almost feel like one long composition, rather than simply a collection of individual songs. The transitions, recurring atmosphere and production choices create an unusually strong sense of unity.From a progressive perspective, I would describe the album as moderately progressive. It is not constantly concerned with complex time signatures, virtuosity or extremely elaborate structures. Instead, its progressive qualities come from the development of ideas, extended instrumental passages, experimentation with sound, thematic coherence and the willingness to let atmosphere become a fundamental part of the composition.The instrumentation is excellent throughout. Gilmour's guitars are a major highlight, Wright's keyboards and synthesizers are perhaps the most distinctive element of the album for me, Nick Mason's drumming contributes effectively to the long developments, and the saxophone adds another color to the sound. The engineering and production are also outstanding, particularly in the way the instruments and effects are separated and integrated into the overall soundscape.The album's strongest qualities are "Shine On You Crazy Diamond," Richard Wright's synthesizers and keyboards, and David Gilmour's guitars and vocals. I honestly don't have any significant weaknesses to point out. Even though "Wish You Were Here" itself is the most commercial track and the one I personally rate lowest, it is still an important part of the complete experience.Overall, Wish You Were Here is an album in which you can become completely absorbed in the atmosphere of the music. It is contemplative, melancholic, psychedelic and emotionally powerful, while remaining carefully composed and remarkably cohesive.Alongside Meddle and Atom Heart Mother, it is among my favorite Pink Floyd albums.Essential for anyone interested in atmospheric and psychedelic progressive rock.
items._genre: progressive rock / psychedelic rock / art rock / space rock
items._cn_summary: 这张1975年的专辑将前卫摇滚、迷幻摇滚、艺术摇滚与太空摇滚融合，营造出沉思、忧郁且充满情感的氛围。制作精良，各乐器在混音中各占其位，Richard Wright的合成器与键盘为整体音色增添了关键层次。核心曲目《Shine On You Crazy Diamond》被视为向Syd Barrett致敬的完整作品，吉他的器乐展开与情感表达俱佳，键盘则构建了迷幻与空旷的氛围。歌曲将失落与怀旧之情融入音乐而不显压抑。《Welcome to the Machine》以合成器织体营造出机械化的工业感，展现了Pink Floyd将录音室制作本身纳入作曲的方式。歌词层面，专辑围绕对Barrett的追忆以及对音乐产业异化本质的批判展开，主题在当下依然具有相关性。《Have a Cigar》由Roy Harper献声，旋律更具亲和力。整体而言，这是一张主题统一、情感深沉的前卫摇滚作品，但在结构创新与跨界实验性上并未走得太远。

items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — The surname Gildenl'w is by no means unfamiliar to us. There's no need to explain why here. But it might be worth dwelling a bit on his first name. Born in Sweden, Kristoffer was the bassist for Pain of Salvation up until the double album *Be* (2004), and like most bassists, his demeanor was more low-key at the time, and his role seemingly less prominent than that of his brother, the frontman. Can we then speak of emancipation? Or simply of a search for another form of personal fulfillment? In any case, in 2003, at the height of the famous progressive metal band's popularity, Kristoffer left Sweden and Pain of Salvation to move to the Netherlands, collaborating on both sides of the Atlantic with some heavyweights of the progressive rock scene (Damien Wilson, Neal Morse, Lana Lane, the band Kayak'), before launching a solo career in 2012 with the album *Rust*.Begun in 2019 (alongside the album *Homebound*), *Empty*, Kristoffer Gildenl'w's fifth and latest solo album, was originally scheduled for 2020, but a devastating pandemic had other plans, and an unexpected *Let Me Be A Ghost* took precedence, releasing in 2021. Despite its overarching theme (depression), the album *Let Me Be A Ghost* still contained beautiful moments of musical serenity, a touch of melodic and harmonic lightness, as if weightless. There was gravity, too, but it knew how to be playful at times. And this ghostly imprint ultimately led to a kind of peace. 'Let Me Be A Ghost' seemed to describe the sensation of falling'but a fall from which one gets back up, with difficulty, not without effort, yet with courage and the feeling of having grown.'Empty' is even more striking because it offers a broader critical perspective on another tragic fall'that of humanity, drawn into the emptiness of our existence. The music thus becomes the anxious echo of a palpable despair that conveys the state of mind of a man struggling not to fall into this void'this vast, searing void that weighs on our hearts, terrified at the thought of what humanity is doing, a lost humanity in search of meaning.Like his previous solo albums, *Empty* possesses the same strange power of attraction'an irresistible pull that draws us entirely into a universe poised between dream and reality, between soothing light and revealing darkness. How can one resist lyrics so beautiful, so poignant'all these words that soar directly toward the heavens, sung in that deep, comforting, instantly recognizable voice that speaks of disarray, doubt, the pain of incomprehension in the face of human beings' self-destructive recklessness'a voice that speaks to us of our fears and sufferings as fragile beings, just as one might speak to a damned soul waiting in vain for its due.Despite all, one senses the presence of a mystery'a reflection on our purpose in life'carried by Kristoffer Gildenl'w's music and the brilliant artists who perform it. Each composition is a bewildering showcase of beauty, set to restrained vocals, but that is precisely what makes Kristoffer's style so powerful and heightens the emotional vertigo it evokes in us. Each track on his album is a profound and expansive anthem that can help us endure all the torments of the world. We can sense echoes of his former band. We can sense his love for Joni Mitchell, Mike Oldfield, and other giants of the '70s. We hear echoes of Anathema or Dire Straits. We encounter heart-wrenching blues ' la Pink Floyd, the kind whose mysteries were known only to Gilmour and Waters when they were still able to get along. It is dark and dense music, yet it regularly lightens, expands, shakes itself free, moves, and brightens'notably thanks to the graceful arabesques of Ben Mathot and Anne Bakker's violins, a rhythm section capable of softening its touch, the enchanting piano arpeggios played by Kristoffer himself, or the memorable feverish surges of the electric guitar tamed by sorcerers who seem to command the waves and the flames; all these warm notes like so many stars burning eternally to soothe our nights.*Empty* is one of those rich and profound progressive rock works that give us all the more the more we bring of ourselves to them as we receive them'intuitively felt by the heart yet always surprising to the ear. By giving us the best of himself here'which requires great courage' Kristoffer Gildenl'w sets an example by casting an intense light into the night of our troubled souls, illuminating with irrepressible hope a reality before which the malevolent structures of our destructive imagination and our death-dealing impulses dissolve'the only true light, the one that seeks to purify us of our unforgivable sins committed against Mother Nature. In the end, 'Empty' is neither sad nor despairing. In any case, even in the face of impending disaster, there will always be something good to take away'if only a tiny drop of happiness or a pinch of love.
items._genre: crossover prog / progressive rock / art rock
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是瑞典音乐人Kristoffer Gildenlöw的第五张个人作品，跨越多年录制，主题围绕人类存在的空虚与绝望展开，音乐承载了沉重的哲学反思。评论追溯了音乐人离开Pain of Salvation后的个人历程，将其独奏生涯定位为对自我表达的追寻。专辑延续了他一贯的特质——深沉的嗓音、诗化的歌词，以及介于梦境与现实之间的音乐氛围。每首作品被视为对生命目的之思考的载体，由多位出色的乐手共同演绎。整体而言，这是一张内省型的前卫摇滚作品，以忧郁但不失光亮的情绪基调探讨人类困境。

items.body: Cold Spring releases SATØRI’s “Your Life Is Worth Nothing” on 2 October 2026, on CD in a matt-laminate digipak under catalog number CSR364CD. The album mixes harsh industrial noise and power electronics with hard, heavy beats, hostile vocals and dark electronics, and is priced at £9.49 in advance, rising to £11.49 after release. SATØRI’s eleven tracks on ‘Your Life Is Worth Nothing’ The album runs eleven tracks, recorded and mixed by Dave Kirby at Digitalis in Somerset across 2025 and 2026, mastered by Martin Bowes at The Cage Studios, with artwork by Abby Helasdottir: “Last Rites” (3:58) “Perverseverence” (3:47) “Don’t Bend: Break” (4:38) “Suck Out The Light” (3:52) “Seeds Of Darkness” (7:44) “Growing Violence” (6:09) “Trajan” (3:49) “Shattered” (3:52) “Haunted” (4:46) “Pillars Of Salt” (4:47) “Can’t Stop The Itch” (6:30) Track ten shares its title with SATØRI’s previous Cold Spring album, “Pillars Of Salt”, released in 2025. Your Life Is Worth Nothing by Satøri SATØRI described the album’s themes directly: “They think it. Sometimes you think it. A black oppression that takes over; consuming your very soul. The pointlessness of existence. Your single-minded fight against a world and what seems to be an entire population who invalidate everything you believe or stand for, create a climate in which you struggle to survive and destroy the opportunities for you to ever fulfil your potential. Remember: your life is worth nothing.” SATØRI live dates 2026 03.10.2026 – Glossop, UK – The Globe – album launch, with T.A.G.C. (Adi Newton of Clock DVA), Colossloth and Llyn Y Cwn 07.11.2026 – Barnstaple, UK – St Anne’s – with Colossloth and A Waste Of Damnation Side-Line has previously covered the Glossop date, where the album launch sits alongside Colossloth’s own new-album show and a T.A.G.C. set from Adi Newton. About SATØRI SATØRI formed in Margate, Kent, in 1984, when Dave Kirby and Robert Maycock began recording as Psychopath, adopting the name Satori in 1987, the same year Cold Spring-affiliated label Broken Flag released the project’s self-titled cassette. Further tapes followed on Mindscan Tapes through the late 1980s and into the early 1990s, including “Behold The Past”, “Power Of The Gun” and the “Techno Primitive” release credited to Satori Soundsystem. Maycock left in late 1993, Justin Mitchell joined in 1994, and the band disbanded in 1996. Mitchell revived Satori in 2006 with Neil Chaney, and the pair toured Japan alongside Sutcliffe Jugend in April 2007. Cold Spring picked up the project in 2008, releasing the album “Contemptus Mundi” and the CD edition of “Kanashibari” (its LP version had appeared in Japan on Dogma Chase earlier that year), alongside a split release with Merzbow and Sutcliffe Jügend and another with Nadja and Atavist. Dave Kirby, the sole constant member since 1987, resumed the project alone in 2014 and later began spelling the name SATØRI. Cold Spring has released two SATØRI albums under that spelling before the new record: “The Woods” in 2023 and “Pillars Of Salt” in 2025, making “Your Life Is Worth Nothing” the label’s third SATØRI album since Kirby’s solo return. The launch show for the new record takes place on 3 October 2026 at The Globe in Glossop, alongside album launches from Colossloth and a T.A.G.C. set from Adi Newton.

items.body: More than twenty years after Agonoize emerged from Berlin, there is very little ambiguity left about what the name represents. The band built its identity around severe electronic rhythm, distorted vocals, confrontation and a live language that made physical excess part of the music rather than decoration around it. Their own terminology, Hellektro, became closely associated with the harder end of dark electro and aggrotech, combining EBM, industrial and dark-electronic structures with an unusually direct lyrical vocabulary. Agonoize themselves have never seemed especially interested in respecting the borders of those labels. That history also explains why a short conversation with Chris L in 2026 becomes more interesting than a routine tour update. The existing catalogue carries considerable weight, the visual mythology of the band is instantly recognisable, and songs written years ago remain embedded in club culture. But Chris is not speaking about preservation. After a serious illness interrupted both his physical momentum and his songwriting, he is working on new Agonoize material again, while approaching the band with a strikingly uncomplicated principle: he still makes music because he wants to. Ahead of Agonoize’s 25 September appearance at Klub Łącznik in Wrocław, where they play alongside System Noire and Antibody, I caught up with Chris L about returning to songwriting, refusing genre boxes, anger as creative material, performing after illness and why getting older has done very little to make Agonoize more polite. The Wrocław event features full sets from Agonoize and System Noire, with Antibody as special guest and an Angst Factor aftershow with DJane Nox Occultae and DJ Bjørn. Chris L on Agonoize in 2026 Karo: Agonoize have existed for more than two decades now. What does the band need to mean to you personally in 2026 for it still to be worth continuing? Chris: Why shouldn’t it be worth it? I make music because I love it. That’s really the most important reason. As long as I still have something to say and the passion to do it, it will always be worth continuing. Karo: “Revelation Six Six Sick” is already five years old. Are you actively working towards a new Agonoize chapter, and if so, what has changed in the way you want the band to sound? Chris: Five years ago, I was knocked off my feet by a serious illness. It took a long time to find the strength and inspiration to write new songs again. Now I’m working on new material. Time will tell… Karo: “Adios, Goodbye!” with Antibody was one of the more recent glimpses of your writing outside the existing Agonoize catalogue, and now you are sharing the stage in Poland. Did that collaboration open any ideas you would actually like to take further? Chris: “Adios, Goodbye” is not a musical composition by Agonoize. It’s simply a lyric I wrote. The finished song then sat unused for more than a year, for whatever reason. Jan from Antibody is a permanent part of Agonoize, but this song has nothing to do with the Agonoize album that is currently in the works. Karo: Aggrotech has gone through periods of enormous visibility and others when people almost seemed embarrassed by the term. Do you still identify strongly with that scene, or has Agonoize outgrown the usefulness of the label? Chris: I’ve never tried to put a specific musical label on Agonoize. Agonoize is Agonoize. We make our music the way it feels right to us, and I’ve never been interested in putting the band into a box. Karo: I first saw you at WGT many years ago, when there was literally a warning that “there will be blood on the dancefloor.” Back then, the provocation felt genuinely confrontational. Has your own relationship with shock and theatrical violence changed as both you and the audience have grown older? Chris: Agonoize has always been known for addressing subjects that other people don’t dare to talk about. I’m loud, I’m uncomfortable, and I think that’s a good thing. Being different has always been important to me. I don’t have to please everyone. I am who I am. And that has nothing to do with age either. Our fans range from 8 to 70 years old. Music doesn’t have an age limit. Karo: A show with such a recognisable visual language can eventually become something audiences expect rather than something that unsettles them. How do you stop an Agonoize concert from turning into a ritual recreation of its own mythology? Chris: The lyrics I write speak a very clear language and create a very clear picture. I don’t want to hide things behind unnecessary metaphors or sugarcoat them. If I have something to say, I say it directly. Karo: Your lyrics have always used anger very directly. What genuinely makes Chris L angry enough to write about in 2026, and has that anger become more focused with age, or less? Chris: Just look at the world around you. Everything that is happening out there becomes part of the stories we write. We live in a terrible world, and in many ways it seems to be getting worse rather than better. There is just as much anger, frustration and darkness in the world as there has ever been. Of course, all of that finds its way into my lyrics and, ultimately, into my music. Karo: You played M’era Luna again this summer and will soon move into a much more immediate club setting in Wrocław. Does the scale of the room actually change the way you perform, or is Agonoize supposed to overwhelm the space regardless of its size? Chris: I’ve always preferred playing small clubs. There’s something special about being close to the audience, with no barriers and no distance between us. That direct connection is what I love about live shows. And ultimately, it doesn’t depend on the size of the venue. We perform in front of 10,000 people with the same intensity as we do in front of 150. Karo: Agonoize have a catalogue full of songs audiences expect to hear. When constructing a set now, how do you balance that collective memory against your own need not to spend the evening reproducing the past? Chris: Every show is different. The combination of old and new songs is important, and that mixture should be something people can feel at every show. In the past, two-and-a-half to four-and-a-half-hour shows were not unusual for me. Because of my illness, that’s unfortunately no longer possible. But a shorter show can still be just as intense and uncompromising. Karo: Looking ahead, what do you want the next phase of Agonoize to prove, not to people who already know exactly what “Bis das Blut gefriert” means to them, but to somebody encountering the band for the first time now? Chris: I have nothing to prove to anyone except myself. I just want to be able to do what I’ve always been best at: making music. Ultimately, that’s all I want. About Agonoize Formed in Berlin in 2002, Agonoize became one of the most recognisable names in the harder European electro scene. Their official biography describes the project through a collision of industrial, EBM and dark electro, while the band has long used the term Hellektro for its own particularly abrasive variant of that language. From the early “Paranoid Destruction” period through records and releases such as “Assimilation”, “Blutgruppe Jesus”, “Bis das Blut gefriert” and the later “Revelation Six Six Sick”, aggression has remained central, but so has Chris L’s insistence on direct language and subjects designed to create discomfort rather than polite distance. Side-Line previously spoke with the band in 2020 for the ‘Click Interview’ with Agonoize. The theatrical violence of the concerts, including the band’s notorious “Blutshow”, became part of that identity, but the interview above suggests something more useful about Agonoize in 2026: beneath all the blood, noise and provocation, the continuation of the band still depends on something remarkably basic, Chris L wanting to write music again. items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是丹麦三人组合GuldGanger的首张数字EP，共收录五首作品。核心人物是北欧民谣界资深歌手Mia Guldhammer，其余两位音乐人以各自的理解重新诠释传统曲目。开场曲《Svennedal》以粗犷的小跑节奏展示主唱嗓音的说服力；唯一的原创曲目《Nordgård》由成员Morten Musicus作曲，口琴与风笛提供了推进感。传统曲《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》中，扬琴带来细腻的底色，主唱的口琴与其他乐器交织出多层次质感。终曲《Ormsø》作为纯器乐曲，以口琴开场，与笛子和弦乐交融，呈现一种不安分却令人兴奋的质地。整体弥漫着古老、吱呀作响的氛围，乐手展现出超越首秀水平的成熟度，为乐队的完整专辑埋下期待。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."

items._cn_summary: 这是一张以芝加哥南区的枪支暴力幸存者口述为核心的声音记录作品，录音在一位九十四岁老祖母家的前廊完成。二十五位年龄从十七岁到六十七岁的参与者讲述亲身经历，编曲者伊恩·布伦南未添加任何音乐，仅保留街头环境声与即兴说唱片段。录音当日恰逢特朗普下令国民警卫队进驻芝加哥，地理上靠近豪华的华丽大道，却是被遗忘的社区。作者放弃了传统乐评的形式，直接引用录音师本人评注与原始素材，强调那些不愿主动开口的讲述者反而最具感染力。一位失去两个儿子的长者情绪崩溃连声道歉，录音并未提供任何音乐性的抚慰。项目收益将捐赠给以公共卫生方法遏制暴力的国际组织。整体更像田野录音与声音档案，而非传统意义上的音乐作品。

items._cn_summary: 本文是Bandcamp Daily关于德国krautrock先驱Faust发行四张新专辑的简要新闻预告。Faust作为1970年代以来的实验摇滚先驱，以其独特的声音实验著称。本期四张专辑各自朝不同方向延伸其标志性声响，延续了乐队一贯的多向实验传统。然而原文仅为极短摘要，内容严重不足，缺乏对各专辑具体音乐手法、制作细节或艺术意图的深入评述，无法获得有效乐评信息。作为krautrock/实验摇滚领域的资深乐队，其音乐与用户偏好的实验/前卫音乐方向有一定关联，但原文信息量极低，且仅为新闻转载性质，评分需大幅下调。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — In 1971, Biblical themes and rock operas were all the rage. This was David's contribution to the phenomenon. Though recorded in LA with a 38-piece orchestra (including bassist Carol Kaye, keyboard specialist Don Randi, and guitarist Mike Deasy), the lead vocalists are only listed as the singing group "The Dillons" while David's friend Julian "Cannonball" Adderley politely serves as the album's producer.A1. "Overture" (5:49) the first half is bombastic symphony orchestra, very well composed and rendered--like an overture. At the 2:45 mark there is a stoppage which is slowly filled by wah-wah-electric guitar, electric bass, funk-rock drumming, and dirty/raunchy electric piano as the orchestra horns and strings re-engage, only in more of a support/accent role--though their melodic presentation is continuous of those melodies presented in the opening half. Very cool! Very solid and well-rendered and powerful. (9.5/10)A2. "Comfort Ye My People" (2:45) Elton John-like solo piano opens this before male tenor voice enters to sing the words of the song's title. I really like this arrangement, the way David builds around Ed Dillon's singing and then start to increase in intensity and dramatic effect. (9.125/10)A3. "And The Glory Of The Lord" (4:50) like a rock-orchestra arrangement of a gospel choir rendering of this liturgical song. The vocal arrangements are quite rich and sophisticated; the rock instrumentation a little out of place. (9/10)A4. "Behold" (2:35) led by a Black female Gospel-Blues singer (a Dillon?), acoustic guitar is the only support instrument for the first minute--the first verse. Slow development brings in blues-rock instrumentation with orchestral horn support. Carol Kaye's bass and the electric piano are the most prominent of the rock musicians. Nothing very special or even dramatic here. (8.75/10) B1. "Pastoral Symphony" (5:35) layers of strings open this one, presenting the melody in a kind of fugue before more sections of the orchestra are slowly brought in. This sounds a bit like a New Age "spreading out" of a Pachelbel song. Nice but, again, nothing ground-breaking or exceptional. (8.75/10) B2. "And The Angel Said Unto Them" (2:52) opening with the same orchestral strings, in the second half of the first minute the music eventually gives way to a R&B combo for a Black female soprano gospel singer to sing over. The full orchestra is quite present, serving as thick and integral support, though the drums, bass, electric piano, and electric guitar work are the most active and aggressive here--especially in the song's second half--as anything else on the album. (Could that have been Earl Palmer on the drums?) (9/10) B3. "Glory To God" (3:03) elements of both female and male choirs are presented as opposed, woven, and antiphonal/echoing parts of the lyrical presentation while gentle funk-rock band and full symphonic orchestra participate from start to near-the finish. Quite a disciplined performance that David got out of these singers (as well as the orchestra). (9.125/10)B4. "Hallelujah" (3:23) we all know and love it. This one sounds like a slightly slowed-down, BARRY WHITE-version of the tune--until, that is, the second minute when the music moves into an all-instrumental section where Don, Mike, and the orchestra's horn section are given a little room to express themselves in solos. But then we return to the horn-embellished vocal delivery. I have to admit that I've heard many versions of this "song" that I like far better. (8.75/10)B5. "Worthy Is The Lamb" (2:52) nice Gospel choir music with totally-unnecessary and unfulfilling rock instrumentation. Even the orchestral work on this one feels as if it "gets in the way" of the fine vocal work. "The Dillons" are definitely a fine choir. (8.875/10)Total time: 32:40I have to say that this was one of the few times that I actually thought that the great Carol Kaye's bass playing was unbefitting to the music, which feels really weird since I revere her work and instincts so highly. Where I think David's work--his "Rock Interpretation"--started really strongly, I think it went off the rails somewhere in the middle of the Second Side. B+/4.5 stars; a near-masterpiece of the fusion of rock, jazz, R&B, and classical musical styles.
items._genre: progressive rock / orchestral rock / gospel rock / crossover prog
items._cn_summary: 这张1971年的专辑是David Axelrod对亨德尔《弥赛亚》的摇滚化改编，洛杉矶录制，使用38人管弦乐团搭配放克摇滚乐队编制。乐评详细逐曲分析了管弦乐与摇滚乐器的交织方式，如管弦乐开场后切入哇音吉他、放克鼓点和电钢琴，或以钢琴独奏引入男高音独唱，再如福音女声搭配蓝调摇滚乐器等。制作人Cannonball Adderley参与，演唱由The Dillons组合担纲。整体属于将巴洛克经典作品以摇滚乐队和福音人声重新诠释的跨界尝试，制作精良但风格上更偏向交响摇滚加福音融合，与用户偏好的实验前卫、学院爵士、电子及暗潮等方向距离较远，跨领域融合有限。

items.body: Review by Hector Enrique — In the early 2000s, Savatage's core members were juggling their time and musical ideas between the band and the increasingly demanding side project Trans-Siberian Orchestra, created by Jon Oliva, producer Paul O'Neill, and arranger and keyboardist Robert Kinkel. It was against this hectic backdrop that the American band released "Poets and Madmen" (2001), their eleventh album, whose central theme revolves around a loose adaptation inspired by the tragic fate of Kevin Carter, the photographer who captured the harrowing image of a Sudanese child crouching on the ground, watched from a short distance by a vultur - a photograph that earned him the Pulitzer Prize in 1994.The album features the return of Oliva's raw and expressive voice as lead singer, a greater prominence of Chris Caffery's rhythmic and heavy guitar riffs, and a solid instrumental foundation, supported by Kinkel's symphonic arrangements. All of this lends, on the one hand, that combination of theatrical stage presence and razor-sharp energy characteristic of metal outbursts in tracks like the anguished "Stay with Me a While", the martial "Commissar," and, above all, the epic "Morphine Child", an elaborate and highly fluid epic that includes superb choral segments and is surely the jewel of the album.On the other hand, there's room to revisit the genre's raw, primal roots with the fast-paced, '80s-style heavy track "Drive"; the density of doom metal with Sabbath-esque touches in "I Seek Power" - another great track - ; and the pasty "Awaken," with Oliva on the verge of vocal breakdown. There are also some acoustic subtleties in hybrid tracks like "The Rumour (Jesus)" and "Man on the Mirror", where the band navigates peaceful valleys and abrupt instrumental mood shifts with great skill.The self-indulgent and theatrical "Got to Get Back to a Reason" - a track that attempts to capture the emotion in the air and give the album an epic, redemptive ending - ends up also being the final piece in the band's discography. Because, despite the musicians' intention to maintain both projects simultaneously, their packed schedules and commitments made their coexistence unsustainable. After the album's promotional tour and in the absence of an official statement, Savatage went on a "hiatus" that has now lasted 25 years...3.5/4 stars
items._genre: progressive metal / heavy metal / symphonic metal
items._cn_summary: Savatage第十一张专辑以1994年普利策奖摄影作品为灵感核心，讲述摄影师凯文·卡特在苏丹拍摄秃鹫与饥饿儿童后的悲剧命运。Jon Oliva回归主唱位置，其粗粝而富有表现力的嗓音与Chris Caffery的重型吉他riff形成核心张力，Robert Kinkel的交响编曲为整体提供宏大底色。专辑在风格上呈现多面性：既有舞台剧式的戏剧张力与金属爆发力，体现在《Morphine Child》的史诗合唱段落中；也回溯八十年代速度金属的原始冲击力，以及带有黑色安息日影响的厄运金属密度。acoustic段落与器乐情绪骤转的混合曲目展示了乐队的技术驾驭力。作为乐队隐退前的终章，专辑试图以宏大救赎的尾声收束整个历程。整体而言，这是一张以叙事主题驱动的传统前卫金属作品，与用户的实验、前卫、爵士、电子等偏好领域距离较远。

items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — D'Arcansiel, an Italian band with a French comically misspelled name (all the more strange given that the opening track of their 1988 debut album is aptly titled "Un Arc dans le Ciel"), which emerged in the mid-1980s and disbanded a few years later, we were familiar with their three neo-prog albums (including the quite respectable *Still Searching*, released in 1990), heavily influenced by Marillion from the same era, though none of them left a lasting impression on our minds, already saturated with prog masterpieces of all kinds. Suffice it to say, I wouldn't have bet much on a new Arcansiel album ? I would have been wrong, because that's exactly what just happened with *Hard Times*, an undeniable success in a very personal RPI style that easily makes you forget the band's earlier efforts. This proves once again, as the saying goes, that it's never too late to do things right. "Too Late!" Yet this is the painful cry of alarm delivered?through the voice of the excellent singer Marco Leccese and the band's new keyboardist Davide Sorella?right from the introduction of the first track, a nearly 18-minute suite that Sorella wrote and composed.The state of Planet Earth is cause for concern, and even if it's not certain that the point of no return has been reached, we can safely say that we will not leave this place in the same condition we found it. The beauty of the world is fragile, and humankind is a malevolent shadow that has never ceased to wither it away. Progress continues its rapid march regardless of the circumstances and seems to defy even the most alarming signs. So is it too late to avert disaster? Sorella tells us instead that it's too late to keep wasting our time making bad decisions or failing to take any serious action.Musically, "Too Late" is a grand symphonic prog epic as captivating and inexhaustible as the theme it explores. With a neo-Baroque-inspired leitmotif that gives center stage to a keyboard-dominated instrumental section (a commanding synth, a very assertive piano, a mischievous harpsichord, and a swift Hammond organ playing in rondo form), all in service of hyper-melodic vocal parts?reminiscent of what Oliviero Lacagnina has recently done with The Samurai of Prog, or even Gryphon at their most prog?this majestic epic manages to bathe discreetly in a fluid, slightly jazzy atmosphere, then bursts into a symphony that is more melancholic than desperate, at times bordering on the tragic. After such a fireworks display?18 minutes that seem to fly by in the blink of an eye and that one wishes could last an eternity?the rest might seem to take a back seat, less grandiose. But this impression quickly fades upon listening to the next three tracks, which are just as brilliant."Hard Times" (like the title of Dickens' novel), can be understood as "Difficult Times" but 'Hard' also means "Tough." We are indeed living in an era with problems that are difficult (but not impossible?) to solve on every level (social, cultural, ethical, ecological, political?); but we are also in a world that is hard to live in for many of us?and that "us" encompasses the majority of living beings. Arcansiel's album offers us some enlightening accounts of this. From the scathing and mocking "Puppets and Puppeteers" (a description of one of the most irritating aspects of new media) to the disillusioned "Heaven Is Not Here" (beware of smooth talkers and false promises), the social issues addressed in *Hard Times* are critical reflections that remain relevant and never fail to move the listener.The result of a collaboration between bassist Felice Lombardo and guitarist Sebastiano Valvo, "Puppets and Puppeteers " (7:51) brings a fairly distinct shift in musical atmosphere by adopting a deliberate tempo with irregular measures in a powerful neo-prog style reminiscent of early Asgard (Leccese's vocals play a part in this), illuminated by dazzling synth solos that readily give way to a magnificent lyrical guitar solo. "Heaven Is Not Here" (11:22), written by the bassist, also offers remarkable moments, especially for those who appreciate Jon Anderson's more peaceful work paired with Genesis's "Supper's Ready."Personally, I have a soft spot for the unpredictable "My Old Same Mistakes" (7:27), written by the duo Sorella and Valvo in a melodic style quite similar to the romantic, post-Gabriel era of Genesis, and in which Marco Leccese once again works wonders (his "Save Me," sung with great conviction, is sure to be memorable), though the second half?following a medieval-influenced instrumental bridge?leans toward a swaying jazz-rock style, before concluding with Canterbury-style prog, all seamlessly strung together. As surprising as it is delightful.More than 30 years have passed since *Still Searching*, and only drummer Gianni Lavagno remains to ensure the band's continuity and the legitimacy of the Arcansiel name, though he did not participate in writing the songs for *Hard Times*. The compositions penned by the other three musicians?evolving into a sort of shimmering neo-prog with a distinctly Italian sensibility, featuring numerous twists, breaks, and inspired resurgences?are far richer and more diverse than those of the original Arcansiel. Reusing the same name may seem like a questionable choice, even an abuse of the name. But after all, the label on the bottle isn't very important when it contains such nectar?to be savored without moderation to make our lives sweeter.
items._cn_summary: Arcansiel是一支意大利新前卫摇滚乐队，时隔多年回归推出《Hard Times》。专辑以18分钟的开篇曲为核心，键盘主导的新巴洛克风格主导动机贯穿全曲，融合合成器、钢琴、大键琴与哈蒙德 organ的轮旋曲式，配合高度旋律化的人声，呈现出宏大而略带忧郁的交响性叙事。乐评将其与Marillion、Gryphon及The Samurai of Prog的音乐传统相联系，称赞其个人化的意大利前卫摇滚风格超越了乐队早年的作品。专辑主题关注地球生态危机与人类困境，但音乐表达更倾向于传统交响前卫框架内的精致编排，而非突破性的实验探索。

items.body: Rob Reindorf was an indefatigable Ghanaian powerhouse, who died recently at the age of 77. Unpublished interview and tribute: Filip Kalinowski. Portrait: Sai Galaxy Sampled by J Dilla and Madlib, reissued by Analog Africa and Soundway, the two legendary loose-up-yourself funk albums by Robert Roy “Rob” Reindorf from Ghana – Rob and Make It Fast, Make It Slow – outlived initially being commercial flops on the cut and thrust highlife-driven musical market of Western Africa of the late 1970s. While Rob moved away from the music industry for several decades, European and American crate diggers started to play and edit the eponymous track from his second album to the extent that the album’s price was boosted on Discogs to two and... The post Make it Vast, Make a Show: Remembering Rob appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 本文是对加纳音乐人Robert Roy"Rob"Reindorf的纪念文章，介绍其两张高密度放克专辑《Rob》与《Make It Fast, Make It Slow》。这两张作品在1970年代末西非以高生命音乐为主流的市场中遭遇商业失败，但随后被J Dilla与Madlib采样，并由Analog Africa与Soundway等厂牌再版。文章指出欧洲与美国的唱片挖掘者开始播放并剪辑其第二张专辑中的同名曲目，使该专辑在Discogs上的价格被推高。文章综合呈现了Reindorf作为加纳乐坛重要人物的音乐遗产，以及其在国际采样文化中获得认可的过程。

items._cn_summary: 本文并非传统意义上的深度乐评，而是The Quietus为爱尔兰实验噪音摇滚乐队Gilla Band新专辑《Pugnello》策划的嘉宾歌单一览。文章简述了专辑背景：由乐队成员亲自挑选20首影响作品，涵盖舞曲谜题到鲍勃·迪伦的超现实主义歌词等多元元素，跨越四年录制周期。作为2022年《Most Normal》之后的回归之作，专辑由Rough Trade发行。然而原文以推介形式呈现，未对音乐本体做实质性分析，缺乏声音质感、创作手法或概念深度的讨论，信息量有限。乐队风格涉及噪音摇滚、实验与后朋克的交叉地带，与暗潮、实验音乐偏好有一定交集，但内容浅显，难以据此判断专辑的实际艺术价值。

items.body: SAVAK releases “Door Deals And Debt: An Essential Collection From The First 10 Years” on October 23 via Peculiar Works, alongside Ernest Jenning Record Co. The 14-track compilation gathers material from the Brooklyn post-punk band’s first ten years together, drawing on the catalog built across its seven studio albums to date. The tracklist mixes familiar songs with deeper cuts rather than following a straight singles-only format. Eli Kasan of the Pittsburgh band The Gotobeds wrote the liner notes for the collection and was asked to help pick the tracklist; by his own account on the Bandcamp page, only four of his suggestions made the final cut. Kasan sums up the band’s decade-long run by writing that it amounts to “a decade in and no end in sight.” SAVAK’s ‘Door Deals And Debt’ tracklist The 14 songs on “Door Deals And Debt: An Essential Collection From The First 10 Years” are “Vis-a-Vis,” “No Blues No Jazz,” “Dead Dick,” “How Many Duchesses,” “Reaction,” “Like Gary Wilson Said,” “Paid Disappearance,” “Early Western Traders,” “No Man’s Island,” “Two Lamps,” “Sick Of War,” “Nature Erased,” “Empathy” and “Tomorrow And The Day After.” Door Deals And Debt: An Essential Collection From The First 10 Years by SAVAK SAVAK’s autumn tour dates SAVAK marks the release with a free record release show at Mama Tried in Brooklyn on October 25, then crosses to the UK for a run of November dates: October 25 – Brooklyn, NY – Mama Tried (record release show) October 29 – Norwich, UK – The Holloway October 30 – Newcastle, UK – The Lubber Fiend October 31 – Halifax, UK – Dukes November 1 – Nottingham, UK – The Old Cold Store (JT Soar Fest) November 2 – Oxford, UK – The Library November 3 – Bristol, UK – The Golden Lion November 4 – Birmingham, UK – Centrala November 5 – London, UK – The Old Blue Last November 6 – UK (venue TBA) November 7 – Sheffield, UK – CADS About SAVAK SAVAK formed in Brooklyn in 2015 around guitarists and singers Sohrab Habibion, previously of Obits and Edsel, and Michael Jaworski, previously of The Cops and Virgin Islands. Habibion and Jaworski split songwriting and lead vocals between them. Drummer Matt Schulz, also known for his work with Holy Fuck and Enon, rounds out the band’s current lineup; past lineups have included James Canty, Greg Simpson and Benjamin Van Dyke. The band released its debut album, “Best of Luck in Future Endeavors,” on Comedy Minus One in May 2016. It moved to Ernest Jenning Record Co. for “Cut-Ups” in 2017 and “Beg Your Pardon” in 2018, followed by the 12-inch single “Mirror Maker” in 2019, “Rotting Teeth in the Horse’s Mouth” in 2020, “Human Error / Human Delight” in 2022 and “Flavors of Paradise” in 2024, the latter two co-released with the band’s own label, Peculiar Works. Its seventh album, “SQUAWK!,” followed on May 30, 2025, ten years after the band’s first show. “Door Deals And Debt: An Essential Collection From The First 10 Years,” out October 23, 2026 via Peculiar Works and Ernest Jenning Record Co., draws its tracklist from across that decade.

items.body: The Jesus and Mary Chain and The Psychedelic Furs have announced a co-headline tour of the UK for January 2027, playing eight venues from Leeds to London. Tickets go on sale Friday, September 25, 2026 at 10:00 local time through AEG Presents. The run follows a series of co-headline dates the two bands played across the US in 2024, and marks the first time the pairing has toured together in the UK. Tour dates for The Jesus and Mary Chain and The Psychedelic Furs Tuesday, January 19, 2027 – Leeds, UK – O2 Academy Leeds Wednesday, January 20, 2027 – Edinburgh, UK – Usher Hall Friday, January 22, 2027 – Glasgow, UK – O2 Academy Glasgow Saturday, January 23, 2027 – Manchester, UK – Manchester Academy Monday, January 25, 2027 – Bristol, UK – Bristol Beacon Tuesday, January 26, 2027 – Birmingham, UK – O2 Academy Birmingham Thursday, January 28, 2027 – Brighton, UK – Brighton Dome Friday, January 29, 2027 – London, UK – British Airways ARC Tickets are available through AEG Presents. About The Jesus and Mary Chain The Jesus and Mary Chain formed in East Kilbride, Scotland, in 1983 around brothers Jim and William Reid, who recruited Douglas Hart on bass and Murray Dalglish on drums. Signed to Alan McGee’s Creation Records, the band released the noise-pop single “Upside Down” in 1984 before moving to Blanco y Negro for the 1985 debut album “Psychocandy,” which paired feedback-heavy guitars with pop melodies on tracks including “Just Like Honey.” The band’s biggest UK chart success came with the second album “Darklands” (1987) and the single “April Skies,” followed by “Automatic” (1989), “Honey’s Dead” (1992), “Stoned & Dethroned” (1994) and “Munki” (1998), the band’s last record before splitting in 1999. Jim and William Reid reunited in 2007, playing Coachella and returning to full activity with “Damage and Joy” (2017), their first studio album in 19 years. After signing to Fuzz Club Records and reissuing two catalogue albums, the band released its eighth studio album, “Glasgow Eyes,” on March 22, 2024, its first UK top 10 album since 1988. Side-Line covered the campaign in The Jesus And Mary Chain announce new album ‘Glasgow Eyes’ and reported the album’s release date change in The Jesus and Mary Chain shares new single ‘Girl 71’ and pushes back ‘Glasgow Eyes’ album release to March 22. The current line-up is Jim Reid and William Reid alongside Mark Crozer on bass, Scott Von Ryper on guitar and Justin Welch on drums. The band’s January 2027 UK co-headline run with The Psychedelic Furs follows their joint US dates in 2024. About The Psychedelic Furs The Psychedelic Furs formed in London in February 1977 around vocalist Richard Butler and his brother Tim Butler on bass, initially playing under the names RKO and Radio before settling on their current name. The self-titled debut album followed in March 1980, produced by Steve Lillywhite, and 1981’s “Talk Talk Talk” brought the band its first entry on the US Billboard 200. “Forever Now” (1982), produced by Todd Rundgren, gave the band its first Billboard Hot 100 single with “Love My Way,” and “Mirror Moves” (1984) featured “The Ghost in You” and “Heaven.” The band’s re-recording of “Pretty in Pink” for John Hughes’ 1986 film of the same name became its biggest UK and US hit, followed by “Midnight to Midnight” (1987), “Book of Days” (1989) and “World Outside” (1991), after which the group went on hiatus. Richard and Tim Butler reformed The Psychedelic Furs in 2000 with guitarist John Ashton, and the band released its eighth studio album, “Made of Rain,” on July 31, 2020, its first full-length record since “World Outside.” The current touring line-up is Richard Butler, Tim Butler, Amanda Kramer, Rich Good and Zack Alford. The January 2027 UK tour with The Jesus and Mary Chain follows the two bands’ co-headline shows across the US in 2024.

items.body: This Mortal Coil, the rotating collective of musicians and vocalists assembled by 4AD founder Ivo Watts-Russell, released its second studio album, “Filigree & Shadow,” on 22 September 1986 through 4AD. The double LP turns 40 this year. The album gathered 25 tracks, about half of them instrumental, credited to This Mortal Coil but built around a different set of contributors than the project’s 1984 debut. Ivo Watts-Russell and producer John Fryer recorded and mixed “Filigree & Shadow” at Blackwing and Palladium Studios, with arrangements from Simon Raymonde of Cocteau Twins, cellist Martin McCarrick and engineer John Turner, plus violin and viola from Gini Ball. Dead Can Dance percussionist Peter Ulrich and members of Dif Juz, The Wolfgang Press and Colourbox also appeared on the record. Vocalists including Dominic Appleton of Breathless and Alison Limerick sang cover interpretations of songs by Tim Buckley, Gene Clark, Van Morrison, Colin Newman and Talking Heads. “Filigree & Shadow” reached number 53 on the UK Albums Chart and number 2 on the UK Indie Chart, and it streams on Spotify. About This Mortal Coil Ivo Watts-Russell founded 4AD in London in 1980 and built This Mortal Coil a few years later to record music outside the constraints of a fixed band. In 1983 he brought together Cocteau Twins’ Elizabeth Fraser and Robin Guthrie, Cindytalk’s Gordon Sharp and members of Modern English to re-record two Modern English songs as the medley “Sixteen Days/Gathering Dust.” Its B-side, a cover of Tim Buckley’s “Song to the Siren” sung by Fraser and Guthrie alone, entered the UK Singles Chart at number 66 and led Watts-Russell to build a full album around the same idea. That album, “It’ll End in Tears,” followed in 1984 on 4AD. This Mortal Coil never had a fixed lineup. Watts-Russell and engineer John Fryer were its only constant members, and each record drew on a different group of musicians and singers, most pulled from 4AD’s own roster. “Filigree & Shadow” followed in 1986 as the project’s second album, again produced by Watts-Russell and Fryer, with Simon Raymonde, Martin McCarrick and Gini Ball forming its core backing group and Peter Ulrich among the guest musicians. This Mortal Coil closed its studio run with “Blood” in 1991, on which vocalist Caroline Crawley – whose death Side-Line reported in 2016 – was among the featured singers. After the group’s run ended, Watts-Russell continued the same collaborative approach under the name The Hope Blister from 1998, while Fryer went on to produce and engineer widely across the 4AD roster and beyond. “Filigree & Shadow” turns 40 this year, four decades into a project that treated an album as a collaboration rather than the work of a fixed band.
items._genre: darkwave / dream pop / post-punk / gothic / ambient
items._cn_summary: 这是4AD厂牌旗下集体项目This Mortal Coil的第二张专辑，由厂牌创始人Ivo Watts-Russell主导，召集了Cocteau Twins、Dif Juz、Colourbox等4AD系乐队成员参与录制。专辑收录25首曲目，约半数为器乐作品，编曲核心由Simon Raymonde、Martin McCarrick和Gini Ball构成，并邀请Dominic Appleton等歌手翻唱Tim Buckley、Van Morrison、Talking Heads等人作品。制作以人声层叠、弦乐编排与氛围化器乐为主，延续了4AD标志性的空灵、忧郁质感。从风格定位看，这张作品与暗潮、哥特氛围有交集，但整体更偏向梦幻流行和原声氛围，对追求实验前卫、学院派爵士或电子融合的听众而言，其手法相对传统，创新性有限。

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items._cn_summary: Sean Cooney 来自英国民谣组合 Young 'Uns，以1819年曼彻斯特彼得卢屠杀为题材创作概念专辑。作品以原创叙事民谣为载体，邀请 Eliza Carthy、Sam Carter 等客座乐手参与，辅以历史信件、政治漫画与插图装帧成多媒体项目。歌曲围绕历史事件展开，通过个体视角刻画集会者的期待、骑兵冲击的恐怖与事后哀悼。评论指出 Cooney 嗓音具有说服力，旋律动人且意象考究，三重唱编排构成亮点。在当今多国政府压制抗议的背景下，专辑被视为具有现实意义的提醒。其内容扎实、制作精良，但本质上仍属传统英伦叙事民谣范畴，与用户偏好的实验、前卫、爵士、电子、暗潮等方向距离较远。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items.body: Review by kenethlevine — Knowing that DANDO SHAFT was to add POLLY BOLTON as full time member for their eponymous 2nd album, I would have predicted such an infusion to be just what the doctor ordered for balance and groundedness. Paradoxically, this is a notably superior effort yet the 2 tracks on which she sings are among the weaker entries, not bad at all like the inane "Pass it on" but not nearly the equals of the authentic charms of the TIR NA NOG like ballad "Sometimes"; the lively spiritual endeavor of "Waves upon the ether", the sheer charm of "Whispering Ned", and the jaw dropping prog folk exuberance of "Kalyope Driver", their best by far to this point. The Anglo-Celtic flourishes are better integrated than on the debut even if they insist on weightlessly superficial 30 second interludes. A bonus cut on "An Evening with Dando Shaft" does suggest better things ahead with Ms. Bolton and indeed she may well have helped more than mere credits and front line contributions might imply. As you are discovering this unjustly suppressed talented collective along with me, I can only add that time will tell as we pivot freely through history from our advantage point.
items._cn_summary: Dando Shaft的第二张同名专辑在前作基础上引入女声成员Polly Bolton，评论认为整体品质有所提升，但Bolton主唱的两首曲目反而较弱，远不如'Tir Na Nog'式民谣'Sometimes'、活泼的精神性追求'Waves Upon the Ether'、迷人的'Whispering Ned'以及令人惊叹的前卫民谣佳作'Kalyope Driver'。评论指出专辑在英凯尔特元素融合上比首张更为成熟，但30秒间奏段落显得轻浮表面。虽具备民谣根基与一定的前卫倾向，但整体仍属传统英伦民谣框架内的创作，未能突破至更实验或跨界的领域，缺少对实验声响、即兴或电子元素的探索。Bolton的贡献被视为未来发展的积极预兆，暗示后续作品可能更具深度。

items.body: The Cult released their fifth studio album, “Ceremony,” on 23 September 1991, through Beggars Banquet in the United Kingdom and Sire in the United States. The English rock band, who had started the decade before as the post-punk groups Southern Death Cult and Death Cult, made the record as a two-piece with session players. It turns 35 this year. By the time the sessions began, the touring line-up had gone. Bassist Jamie Stewart retired and moved to Canada after the final leg of the “Sonic Temple” tour in April 1990, and drummer Matt Sorum left to join Guns N’ Roses, leaving vocalist Ian Astbury and guitarist Billy Duffy as the only official members. Todd Hoffman played bass and James Kottak drums on the demos. For the album itself, Mickey Curry returned on drums after his session work on “Sonic Temple,” with Charley Drayton on bass. Richie Zito produced, with Astbury and Duffy co-producing, and also contributed keyboards and harmonium. Benmont Tench played organ, piano and mellotron, Scott Thurston added synthesizer and piano to “If,” Suzie Katayama played cello on “Indian,” and Alex Acuña handled percussion on “Indian” and “Wonderland.” Tommy Funderburk sang backing vocals across most of the record, joined by Donny Gerrard, Mona Lisa and Yvonne St. James on “Sweet Salvation.” Phil Kaffel engineered, Mike Fraser mixed, and George Marino mastered the album at Sterling Sound in New York. Pre-production ran at Oliver Ferrand Studio in Los Angeles and Mates in North Hollywood, with recording at Music Grinder Studios in Hollywood and recording and mixing at A&M Recording Studios. The eleven tracks run 63 minutes and 38 seconds: “Ceremony,” “Wild Hearted Son,” “Earth Mofo,” “White,” “If,” “Full Tilt,” “Heart of Soul,” “Bangkok Rain,” “Indian,” “Sweet Salvation” and “Wonderland.” Astbury and Duffy wrote all of them. “Wild Hearted Son” opens with an excerpt from “The Grass Dance” performed by The American Indian Dance Theatre, and “White” quotes Lawrence Lipton’s 1959 book “The Holy Barbarians,” which Astbury took as the name of his next band in 1996. “Wild Hearted Son” was the first single, followed by “Heart of Soul” in 1992. “White” appeared as a single in Canada only, “Sweet Salvation” was issued in Argentina in 1992 as “Dulce Salvación,” and the title track came out as a promotional single in Spain. The cover photograph, taken by John Running, drew a lawsuit. The parents of the Native American boy pictured on the sleeve sued over the unauthorised use of their son’s image, a case Entertainment Weekly reported on 19 June 1992. The New York proceedings against Warner Bros. Records were dismissed in February 1997 for lack of personal jurisdiction; a separate action filed in the District Court of South Dakota on 10 April 1995 was terminated on 16 May 1995. The dispute held up the record’s release in several territories, with South Korea and Thailand not seeing it until 1992 and Turkey not until the band played Istanbul in June 1993. Alan Forbes handled the art direction and design with the band. “Ceremony” reached number 9 on the UK albums chart, was certified gold by the BPI, and went platinum in Canada. Sources differ on its US peak: Wikipedia’s entry on the album gives number 25 on the Billboard 200, while its entry on the band gives number 34. The Ceremonial Stomp tour took the record through Europe in 1991 and North America in 1992, with Michael Lee on drums, Kinley “Barney” Wolfe on bass and John Sinclair on keyboards. The album streams on Spotify. About The Cult Ian Astbury formed Southern Death Cult in Bradford, Yorkshire, in 1981, with guitarist Buzz Burrows, bassist Barry Jepson and drummer Aki Nawaz Qureshi. They played their first show at the Queen’s Hall in Bradford on 29 October 1981, signed to Situation Two, an offshoot of Beggars Banquet, and released the triple A-side single “Moya” in 1982 before ending after sixteen months with a final Manchester show in February 1983. Jepson went on to co-found Into A Circle with Paul “Bee” Hampshire in 1985. In April 1983 Astbury teamed up with Billy Duffy, who had played in the Nosebleeds alongside Morrissey, then Lonesome No More and Theatre of Hate. The new band, Death Cult, added bassist Jamie Stewart and drummer Raymond Taylor Smith, later known as Ray Mondo, both from the London post-punk group Ritual. Death Cult debuted live in Oslo on 25 July 1983 and released the “Death Cult” EP the same month, with the “Gods Zoo” single following in October. Nigel Preston, previously of Sex Gang Children, replaced Mondo that September. The group shortened its name to The Cult in January 1984, ahead of an appearance on the Channel 4 programme The Tube. “Dreamtime,” recorded at Rockfield Studios in Monmouth with producer John Brand, arrived in September 1984 and reached number 21 in the UK. Preston was dismissed in June 1985 and Big Country’s Mark Brzezicki played the “Love” sessions that July and August; the Steve Brown-produced album reached number 4. Les Warner drummed on the world tour that ran from late September 1985 to June 1986. The follow-up was first recorded as “Peace” with Brown at the Manor Studios in Oxfordshire, then re-cut in New York with Rick Rubin and issued in April 1987 as “Electric,” which also reached number 4. Kid Chaos joined on bass for that tour, with Stewart moving to rhythm guitar. “Sonic Temple,” produced by Bob Rock and recorded in Vancouver between October and December 1988, followed in April 1989 and went gold in the UK and platinum in the US. After “Ceremony,” Astbury and Duffy replaced the touring band in 1993 with Craig Adams of The Mission and drummer Scott Garrett, the line-up that recorded “The Cult” with Bob Rock in October 1994. The band split in March 1995 during a South American tour. Astbury formed Holy Barbarians, whose only album “Cream” came out in May 1996, and released the solo record “Spirit\Light\Speed” in June 2000. Duffy worked with Coloursound alongside Craig Adams and Mike Peters, then Dead Men Walking and Cardboard Vampyres. The Cult reformed in 1999 with Sorum and bassist Martyn LeNoble, signed to Atlantic for “Beyond Good and Evil” in 2001, and went on ice again in late 2002. Astbury spent that second break fronting the surviving members of The Doors in a group billed variously as The Doors of the 21st Century, D21c and Riders on the Storm. He announced his departure in February 2007, stating: “I have decided to move on and focus on my own music and legacy.” The Cult had already reunited in January 2006 with drummer John Tempesta, guitarist Mike Dimkich and bassist Chris Wyse. “Born into This,” produced by Martin “Youth” Glover of Killing Joke, came out on Roadrunner on 16 October 2007. Cooking Vinyl signed the band in May 2011 and released “Choice of Weapon” on 22 May 2012 and “Hidden City” on 5 February 2016, both produced by Rock. James Stevenson replaced Dimkich on rhythm guitar in 2013 and Grant Fitzpatrick replaced Wyse on bass in 2015. Duffy also appeared on Wayne Hussey’s 2020 charity remake of “Tower of Strength,” alongside members of Depeche Mode, The Smiths, The Mission, Gary Numan, etc.. The band signed to Black Hill Records in May 2020, began recording at Rockfield in August 2020 with producer Tom Dalgety, and released “Under the Midnight Sun” on 7 October 2022 with Charlie Jones on bass. On 23 October 2025 the group announced a touring hiatus of undetermined length to concentrate on writing and recording. “Ceremony,” the only album in that catalogue made without a settled line-up, turns 35 this year.

items.body: Review by sgtpepper — Alan Parsons Project continued with their prolific album production in 1979. Despite the concept album being out of favour in the time of more superficial music styles (disco, punk) the band holds on to what they do best - clever songwriting, a couple of well arranged instrumentals and heart-broken ballads. "The Lucifer" offers a promising mildly progressive start loaded with synths. The funky "You lie down with dogs" follows, splendid vocal harmonies and live instrumentation. "I'd rather be a man" is the hardest rocking and loudest song on this release. My main interests in this song lie in the rhythm section (bass). "You won't be there" is a melancholic track which would suit to any post-Beatle 70's output but mainly George.After that, the output gets less memorable and unique, for 2 or songs yet it remains pleasant. "Don't hold back" is a simple catchy pop song.But now we're coming to the brilliant two tracks - the Beach Boys magic loaded "Secret gardens", an instrumental with the melody as strong as the sweeping vocal arrangements and atmosphere a la Pet Sounds. After this level of sophistication, we're faced by one of the strongest APP ballads with dreamy melancholic lyrics and fitting music underscoring the message.Lesley Duncan vocal was a great choice as was the mighty church organ chords which evoke the sense of helplessness in me.Recommended to fans of progressive and well executed pop.

items._cn_summary: Alan Parsons Project 1979年概念专辑《Eve》延续了乐队精巧的制作风格，以合成器铺陈和复杂编曲为骨架，融合柔美的和声与器乐段落。开篇曲目以合成器音色奠定渐进基调，随后进入放克律动与硬摇滚的短暂探索。中段旋律趋于平淡，但后半段两首作品成为亮点：一首器乐曲借鉴海滩男孩式精致管弦编配，另一首忧郁民谣以教堂管风琴烘托人声，展现乐队对情绪层次的处理能力。整体制作精良但风格保守，缺乏实验性突破，属主流艺术流行与软摇滚范畴。

items.body: Review by ZowieZiggy — D(evice) - V(oice) - D(rum). or DVD...On this live release, Livgren will not be playing, unfortunately.When looking at the track list, the veteran Kansas fans must be very pleased : several of their anthems are played and lots of good songs are featured as well.In terms of old song, "Belexes" the first track (if you exclude the intro) brings us back to their first release. It is not my fave one from this very good DVD. But it was probably a hint to the audience that they were going to get a very nice Kansas night. And indeed they will! One song could have been avoided without hurting the ensemble : "The Preacher" that I really can't stand (this choir stuff is just too much). Some other ones are just below par, like "Fight Fire with Fire" and "Play the Game Tonight". My favorite songs on this live DVD do belong to their long ones. Both "Icarus", "Song for America" of course (my all time fave), "Journey from Mariabronn", "Cheyenne Anthem","Miracles Out of Nowhere (6:31), The fabulous meddley "Portrait/Pinnacle" & even the extended "Carry on Wayward Son" (just below 10 minutes).This DVD is very good.One can see how the audience likes it, enjoys it and participates.Only a few great songs are missing ("Incomudro") , and Walsh's voice is not always super. Those are the little defects. Four stars.

items.body: Devoted BJ released the single “Ich kann nicht schlafen” on September 11, 2026, through KL Dark Records. Devoted BJ brings a sound that mixes dark pop and pop dance with 80s-style electro synths and industrial percussion. “Ich kann nicht schlafen” is Devoted BJ’s second single of 2026, following “Schatten in der Nacht”, which the same label issued on June 26, 2026. The new track marks a further step in his development as a songwriter alongside the same synth-driven sound, and a further single is already in the works. Beyond Spotify, the single is also available for download through Apple Music, Beatport and Amazon. KL Dark Records and ‘Ich kann nicht schlafen’ KL Dark Records operates as both an artist agency and a label, working across synth pop, dark pop, dark electro, EBM, body pop, gothic, dark wave and industrial. About Devoted BJ Devoted BJ released the “Space Time Energy RMX” EP five years before “Ich kann nicht schlafen.” His return to new material began in 2026 with “Schatten in der Nacht,” issued through KL Dark Records on June 26, and continued on September 11 with “Ich kann nicht schlafen,” released through the same label. A further single is already planned. No other biographical detail beyond the label’s own material could be independently verified at the time of writing.

items.body: Winter Sect will release “Graveyard Girl” on October 2, 2026 on Bandcamp and streaming platforms, a new single from the Washington, D.C. goth rock band’s upcoming EP, “Offering.” The track follows “Say Goodbye,” released earlier in 2026. The sound of ‘Graveyard Girl’ Where “Say Goodbye” leaned into darker territory, “Graveyard Girl” keeps its post-punk backbone but loosens up, pulling in funk bass lines, garage grit, indie pop hooks and a touch of bossa nova rhythm. Singer, lyricist and keyboardist Heather Wayward said the song came together almost by accident during a rehearsal setup: “The song pretty much started with Claudia grooving out on a bass line. It was catchy and I thought let’s do something completely different and not so serious and macabre. First the hook was discovered and we built from there. So with that funk of a groove my mind started walking. Where? Through the graveyard of course. It came together in a cool way and a little twist at the end just makes it fun.” About Winter Sect Winter Sect was formed in late 2023 by California native Claudia Neuman and guitarist Anthony Piazza, both members of DC/Baltimore post-punk band Sister Ex, to pursue a feedback-drenched sound spanning goth, new wave, industrial and psychedelic music with a dark, theatrical rock presentation. The lineup is rounded out by Heather Wayward on keys and vocals and drummer Darryl J. Dardenne, with Neuman also on bass and vocals. The band released two singles, “Mystic Twin” and “Haunted House,” in 2024, followed by “Say Goodbye” in 2026. “Graveyard Girl” will appear on the band’s upcoming EP, “Offering.”
